subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored per-session `/exec` defaults be allowed to loosen the current global or per-agent exec security policy after config changes?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests make persistent session overrides intentional, but the reported behavior affects an exec security boundary and changing precedence would be a compatibility-sensitive policy decision.

options.title: Make config hardening authoritative
options.body: Treat global/per-agent exec security as an upper bound for stored session overrides, add regression coverage, and provide a reset or doctor path for existing persisted exec fields.

options.title: Keep persistent session overrides
options.body: Preserve the current contract and improve docs/diagnostics so operators use tool policy deny or session reset when they need to revoke old `/exec` defaults.

options.title: Add reset without precedence change
options.body: Keep `/exec` precedence as-is but add an operator-visible way to clear stored exec defaults for selected sessions or channels.

recommendation.title: Make config hardening authoritative
recommendation.body: Treat global/per-agent exec security as an upper bound for stored session overrides, add regression coverage, and provide a reset or doctor path for existing persisted exec fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant `/exec` session override contract and later exec-default resolution work trace most clearly to steipete's commits.
